title: [wish] bluetoothsignal strength
line: The Bluetooth widget's device details now show the signal strength, like Wi-Fi networks do.
explanation: The Bluetooth widget never showed signal strength, although BluezQt already exposes each device's RSSI to QML. BlueZ only reports RSSI while the adapter is discovering (for example while the Add Device wizard is searching) and drops it afterwards; connected devices get no RSSI over D-Bus at all. The change adds a "Signal Strength" row to the expanded device details whenever an RSSI is known, converted to a percentage with NetworkManager's Wi-Fi mapping (-100 dBm = 0%, -50 dBm = 100%), and keeps it updated while the details are open.

commits.message:
applet: show signal strength in device details

The applet gave no way to tell how far a device is, unlike Wi-Fi in the
network applet. The device details now show the signal strength as a
percentage whenever BlueZ reports an RSSI, which it does while scanning.

BUG: 478431

media.caption: Master: a paired speaker seen at -62 dBm while scanning; its details show no signal strength
Patched: the same details now end with "Signal Strength: 76%"
Live: the RSSI drops to -90 dBm and the row updates to 20% (left); BlueZ drops the RSSI and the row disappears (right)

reviews.text: This patch does not meaningfully fulfill the wishlist request and introduces nearly unreachable UI in the Bluetooth applet. As noted in the explanation itself, BlueZ only reports Device1.RSSI while actively discovering and never for connected devices, yet the applet only lists paired/connected devices and does not perform discovery, so the Signal Strength row will never appear when using a connected device and almost never when opening the applet normally (nor when searching in bluedevil-wizard, which was untouched). Closing BUG 478431 with this change would be misleading.
changes: Do not merge this as a fix for BUG 478431; the applet details row is effectively dead UI in normal usage because the applet does not run discovery and BlueZ does not expose RSSI for connected devices over D-Bus.

To address the 'when searching' part of the wish, display signal strength in the Add Device pairing wizard (bluedevil-wizard) where discovery is actually active and RSSI is populated, and avoid hardcoding BluezQt's internal -32768 sentinel in QML.

For connected devices, acknowledge the BlueZ D-Bus limitation upstream (or use an API that actually provides connected-device RSSI) rather than closing the wishlist item without supporting connected devices.

reviews.text: The reporter wants signal strength 'when searching or using a Bluetooth connection'. This patch only adds a details row in the applet. The applet lists only paired/connected devices and never scans itself, and BlueZ gives no RSSI for connected devices, so the row only shows for a paired, disconnected device while some other tool (wizard or KCM) happens to be discovering. In normal use the user will almost never see it. The 'searching' case, where it matters most (choosing a device in the Add Device wizard, which already sorts by RSSI but doesn't show it), is not covered, and the 'using a connection' case isn't addressed, so BUG: would close the wish while covering only a corner of it.
changes: Show the signal strength where devices are searched for, i.e. in the Add Device wizard's discovered-device list (and the KCM's pairing list if it has one), not only in the applet's paired-device details.
For connected devices, either get connection RSSI from BlueZ (no D-Bus API today, so it needs upstream work) or use CCBUG and explain the limitation in the MR, instead of BUG: on a partial fix.
Minor: replace the __rssi/on__RssiChanged helper with a normal readonly property or a Connections on model.Rssi, and say in the MR why the Wi-Fi dBm-to-percent mapping is reasonable for Bluetooth.
